marks.gloss_en: the one who says the spice-merchants' hammer [may be used], all the more so the goldsmiths'
the one who says goldsmiths': but the spice-merchants' [hammer], one is particular about it
כיון דשמעה להא דאמר רב חיננא בר שלמיא משמיה דרב: הכל מודים בסיכי זיירי ומזורי, דכיון דקפיד עלייהו מייחד להו מקום -- הא נמי
having heard Rav's הכל מודים בסיכי זיירי ומזורי: הא נמי מייחד להו מקום -- the pestle, like the launderers' pins, has a designated place, so all agree it is not moved (= p_eli_meyached_makom)
(entertained by Rabba) the pestle mishna's ושוין, too, is R' Nechemya's
איתיביה אביי לרבה: an empty mortar may not be moved -- a vessel whose function is prohibited is forbidden even for another use
a mortar: if there is garlic in it, one may move it
הא מני -- רבי נחמיה היא, דאמר אין כלי ניטל אלא לצורך תשמישו (= p_medocha_r_nechemya)
Rabba: whose is this [ruling on the mortar]? It is R' Nechemya's
איתיביה: ושוין שאם קיצב עליו בשר שאסור לטלטלו -- even Beit Hillel forbid moving the pestle afterwards, so a vessel whose function is prohibited is forbidden for another use
Beit Shammai: one does not take the pestle to cut meat on it
a thing whose function is prohibited is permitted [to move] for its own use
R' Yochanan: it is of the goldsmiths' hammer that we learned [the mishna]
תניתוה: מחט של יד ליטול בה את הקוץ -- and what does the thorn care whether it is pierced or not? So a needle without its eye may be used and moved
the mishna: [one may take] a hand needle to take out a thorn with it
מנא אמינא לה, דתנן: אין עושין אפיקטויזין בשבת
Rav Nachman: aligning an infant's limbs on Shabbat is forbidden
איתיביה: מחט שניטל חררה או עוקצה טהורה -- it is pure [no longer a vessel], so how may it be moved?
a needle whose eye or point was removed is pure

טומאה אשבת קרמית?! impurity requires a vessel of work, Shabbat something fit, and this is fit to take out a thorn (= p_tumah_kli_maaseh, p_shabbat_midi_dechazi, p_nitla_chazya_kotz). Rava (123a.15) rejects this answer -- מאן דקמותיב שפיר קמותיב -- which the schema cannot attach to the answer; see header
for impurity we require a vessel of work
מיתיבי: a needle pierced or not may be moved on Shabbat, and 'pierced' was said only regarding impurity -- so a needle's impurity status does not govern Shabbat
a needle, whether pierced or not, may be moved on Shabbat

תרגמה אביי אליבא דרבא: the baraita speaks of unfinished needles, which one may decide to use as they are; a needle whose eye or point was removed is thrown among the junk (= p_golmei_machatin, p_golmei_nimlach, p_nitla_zorkah_legrutaot)
Abaye, according to Rava: [the baraita] speaks of unfinished needles
a needle whose eye or point was removed may be moved on Shabbat (Rava brei deRabba's question; Rav Yosef's answer)
Rava: since for impurity it is not a vessel, for Shabbat too it is not a vessel

והאמר רב נחמן: האי פוגלא... ממטה למעלה אסיר -- Rav Nachman forbids pulling out the radish when it would move the earth, so for him indirect moving IS moving (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara for want of a kind)
הדר ביה רב נחמן מההיא -- Rav Nachman retracted the radish ruling
(the stam's inference) Rav Nachman holds that moving a thing indirectly does not count as moving
the mishna: [one may take] the reed and the shuttle [to stick into food]
R' Elazar ben Tadai: one inserts a reed or a shuttle into them, and they are shaken off by themselves
